title: Expectation interest
summary: The expectation interest places the injured party in the position performance of the promise would have produced, subject to the rules limiting recovery.
notes:
In Hawkins, compare the promised hand with the actual hand; ordinary pain of the contemplated operation was part of the performance the patient agreed to undergo. In Naval Institute, the court estimates the publisher’s lost hardcover profits rather than automatically awarding every profit the breacher earned. Later cases address completion cost, lost profits, mitigation, foreseeability, certainty, and agreed remedies. Define the promised position and account for avoided costs before selecting a dollar measure.

Identify the promised performance, the actual position, avoided costs, and other qualifying losses before adding figures. Hawkins compares the promised and actual hand; Naval Institute estimates sales profits lost because of premature sales. A gain to the defendant is not automatically the claimant’s expectation loss. The Sullivan posture shows why different interest measures can share some components. The early chapters introduce these distinctions without supplying the course’s later complete rules on damage limitations.
